not_found: Individual directly measured 2 3S1-2 3P0 and 2 3S1-2 3P2 absolute frequencies (Cancio Pastor 2004 table): the PRL table is paywalled and the erratum abstract carries no numbers; the two values given here are derived from Zheng 2019 (2 3S1-2 3P1) plus Zheng 2017 intervals.

Measured lifetime / linewidth of 2 3P (1.626 MHz) and of 3 3P (389 nm): no modern direct lifetime measurement located; 97.89 ns is the value tabulated in the Vassen review (equals NIST 1/A). NIST ASD A values (accuracy AAA, theory of Drake) remain the reference for A and matrix elements of 1083, 389, 587.6 and 706.7 nm.

2 3S1-3 3P1 and 2 3S1-3 3P2 (389 nm cooling component) absolute frequencies and the 3He-4He isotope shift at 389 nm (Marin et al. 1995): only the 3 3P0 component (Pavone 1994 abstract) could be opened.

3He hyperfine structure of 2 3P: not describable by simple A, B constants (hyperfine and fine structure are comparable); the seven measured 3He 2 3S-2 3P hyperfine component frequencies are stored on the 1083 nm transition instead. Measured 2 3P hyperfine intervals themselves were not located.
Absolute g_J of 2 3S1: only the measured ratio to g_J(H) is recorded (Drake et al. 1958); g_J values of 2 3P_J not found.
3He 2 3P-3 3D and 3 3D hyperfine separations (Luo et al. 2016): numbers are in the paywalled article body, not in the abstract.
Reduced dipole matrix elements from experiment: none found for helium (theory/NIST only).
conflicts: 4He 2 3S-2 3P centroid: Zheng et al. 2017 276 736 495 600.0(1.4) kHz vs Cancio Pastor et al. (2004 + 2006 erratum) 276 736 495 649.5(2.1) kHz, a 49.5 kHz (about 20 sigma) discrepancy; the original 2004 abstract printed 276 736 495 624.6(2.4) kHz. Zheng (as corrected in PRA 99, 032506) is used for the entries; the 4-3 centroid isotope shift uses the two Florence values so that common systematics cancel.
2 3P1-2 3P2 interval: Kato et al. 2018 2 291 176 590(25) Hz (microwave FOSOF) vs Zheng et al. 2017 2 291 177.56(19) kHz (laser), 0.97 kHz apart (about 5 sigma).

2 3P0-2 3P2 interval: Heydarizadmotlagh et al. 2023 31 908 131 608(65) Hz vs Zheng et al. 2017 31 908 130.98(13) kHz and Smiciklas & Shiner 2010 31 908 131.25(30) kHz; the 2023 paper notes 'large disagreements with previous measurements'.
3He 2 3S1(F=3/2)-2 1S0(F=1/2): van der Werf et al. 2023 192 504 914 418.96(17) kHz vs van Rooij et al. 2011 192 504 914 426.4(1.5) kHz (7.4 kHz, about 5 sigma).
2 3S1 ionization energy: experiment 1 152 842 742.7082(55)(25) MHz (Clausen 2025) vs alpha^7 m theory 1 152 842 742.231(52) MHz (Patkos et al.), 9 sigma.

2 3P1-3 3S1 (706.7 nm): Thomas et al. print 424 202 774(5) MHz for '2 3P1 -> 3 3S1', 2.02 GHz below the NIST Ritz value; the number matches 2 3S1-3 3S1 minus the 2 3S-2 3P centroid. The entry uses the value derived with the 2 3S1-2 3P1 frequency (424 204 793(5) MHz) and keeps the printed one as a not-verified alternative.
2 3S1 lifetime: Hodgman's abstract and text give 7870(510) s; some indexing snippets show 7920(510) s, which is not what the article prints.
notes: Frequencies are 4He unless a key ends in _3 or 'isotope' says 3. 4He has I = 0 (no hyperfine structure); 3He frequencies are single hyperfine components or centroids as stated in each note, never silently centre-of-gravity. Isotope-shift keys 'A-B' mean nu(A) - nu(B). The 2 3P fine-structure intervals are stored on the 2 3P1 and 2 3P0 levels (fine_structure_splitting_MHz; use value_Hz_str for full precision). NIST energies copied from data/he/levels.csv (NIST ASD); the 2 3P order is inverted (J=2 lowest). Entries marked '(abstract)' were read on the publisher's abstract page only. Ionization energies are given as E_I/h in MHz for the excited states and in cm^-1 for the ground-state limit.
